data.narrative:
Silicon Box, a Series B semiconductor frontier-tech company founded by Han Byung Joon, Sehat Sutardja, and Weili Dai, is evaluated against a peer universe of 11 private and 3 public semiconductor companies operating at similar or adjacent funding stages.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the company's $200M+ total capital raised and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $380M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series A), Etched ($5.0B, Series C), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series C), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—yields a $2.0B median with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trade at a 21.4x sector P/S median but cannot be applied without the target's revenue, which remains undisclosed.

Triangulating the stage-progression and peer-median methods produces a valuation range of $323M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The substantial spread reflects the wide dispersion in peer valuations and stage heterogeneity within the semiconductor frontier-tech cohort. Key uncertainties center on revenue traction, technical differentiation relative to named peers, and whether near-term funding trajectory aligns with the 1.9x step-up assumption.
